lines.text: You check the weight twice. Your kind always did.
My kind?
Old men. What did you think I meant?
Hester Quimby tell you I owe her for a coat?
She mentioned it.
I've paid for that coat three times. She keeps sending it back.
That wall of yours is running up quite a bill.
What bill?
Figure of speech. Are you buying that or just holding it?
You've ink on your cuff.
Eldwin looks. There is nothing on his cuff.
My mistake. Light's poor back here.
That beetle still at it?
Every time I look.
Good. I'd hate to have to do it myself.
You've traded with me long enough that I ought to warn you about me.
Go on, then.
That was it. That was the warning.
You're by here more than you used to be. Knees or conscience?
Both, I should think.
Ruth liked this spot. Had me sit here with her every evening for thirty-one years. I never cared for it.
And now?
Now I've got the habit. Don't make anything of it.
My father said there was a warden before you. Went up the mountain one winter and the frost stopped coming down.
Did he say that.
Nobody thought to ask after him till spring. You'd think we'd have asked.
He wouldn't have wanted the fuss.
Knew him, did you?
Eldwin looks up at the wall for a while, and doesn't answer.
Forty years I've watched you go up that road. You've looked the same the whole time, near enough.
It's the beard.
It is not the beard.
Have you eaten? Don't answer. You've got the look of a man about to lie to me.
Twenty autumns I've told you that step wants mending. You'll be dead before you see to it.
Very likely.
Well, don't be. Who would I shout at?
Silas says your lamp was lit till morning.
You'd tell me, wouldn't you? If it was the sort of thing a person ought to be told.
You'd be the first, Ada.
She looks at him a moment longer than she needs to. Then she goes back to the pies.
He sits at the top of your stairs when you're up at the walls. Won't eat till you're back. Then he eats everything.
He's a cat, Ada.
I know what he is. I'm telling you what he does.
Ada's crust is too thick. You can tell her I said so.
No. Don't.
Asked her once, you know. Nineteen years back. She said ask again when that press stops leaking.
It's running sweet as June.
I know it is. I've been meaning to loosen something.
Went over there this morning. Had the whole thing worked out.
And?
I've got a lot of pie.
My mother played "Soldier's Joy" at her own wedding. Said it beat listening to my father.
I go up and play to the wall some mornings. Don't tell the minister.
It doesn't clap. It doesn't ask for "Soldier's Joy", either.
That tune from the wall won't finish. Gets near the end and I can't find how it goes.
Eldwin hums four notes.
That's it. That's how it goes. I haven't played that for a soul. Where did you hear it?
It's an old tune, Abigail.
She looks up toward the wall, and doesn't ask him anything else.
That long boy brings Lydia apples now. He brings them to my door and stands there holding them.
I've started taking them. We can't have him standing there all winter.
She slept on my feet last night. I couldn't feel them, and I didn't move.
I asked Mama how long geese live. She said long enough. That's what she said about Grandpa.
Mrs. Applegate strikes me as someone who will decide that for herself.
Mrs. Applegate laid an egg. I'm not allowed to say where.
I shan't ask.
It was in the minister's hat.
Between ourselves, Eldwin, I have been giving the same sermon for nineteen years. I move the harvest about.
I have forgiven the goose. I told her so. She bit me again, so we will need to go over it.
The man before me left the sermon book and one note. 'Give thanks for the autumn and do not ask.' I took it for a joke.
Did you ask?
Who would I ask?
My mother stitched that little wizard in the corner. I've mended him twice. He's worn better than you.
That brown square was Amos Tuttle's boy's. Every year Amos gives it and says nothing, and I sew it in and say nothing.
You do have a long memory, Martha.
That's what the needle's for.
Still wrong. I keep meaning to fix it. It's a comfort, having an hour nobody else has got.
My boy used to wind it. Stood on a chair to reach.
I remember. He had a good hand.
He did, didn't he.
Granddad said he set every stone from the church to the mill. You've seen the walls. Would you say he was lying?
I'd say he set a good many.
That flask I gave you's got a bend in it. Forty years on his hip. You can't drink from it without leaning.
I can't write to her now. She reads them for spelling.
We danced. I counted out loud. She said she liked it. I don't think she did. I think she likes me anyway. Is that allowed?
It's the usual arrangement.
Pa asked if I'd seen his coat. I said no. It was standing right behind him.
Somebody's moved my scarecrow over by the wall. I asked Pa. I asked Caleb.
I don't like asking people things.
Deacon came second in the pull. There were two oxen. He doesn't know. I'd thank you not to say.
He'll be done in a year or two. I've been thinking what I'd say to him.
Haven't got anything. We never needed it.
Mister Rook says you're older than the church.
Mister Rook says a great many things.
That's not no.
Mama says I can go past the bridge when I'm bigger. How big were you?
About your size, I should think. I went anyway.
I'm not telling her you said that.
I know two notes now. One's an accident.
He tell you he paid for that coat?
Three times, he says.
Three times, yes. Three different things, and none of them his to give.
